content.title: About
content.content: Canned lentil soup with reduced sodium is a ready‑to‑eat product made from selected red or green lentils, vegetables, and spices. The lower salt level makes it suitable for people monitoring their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lentils are one of the oldest legumes, cultivated for over 8,000 years.
Canning preserves nutrients and flavor without the need for refrigeration.
Reduced sodium is achieved by replacing part of the salt with herbs and spices such as thyme and bay leaf.
Lentil soup is often used in weight‑loss diets because of its high protein and fiber content.
In many cultures, lentil soup is a traditional dish during fasting periods.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Lentils provide about 9 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and promotes gut health.

items.title: Low sodium content
items.content: Reduced salt helps control blood pressure and reduces strain on the cardiovascular system.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron supports oxygen transport, while folate is essential for DNA synthesis and pregnancy health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients in lentils combat free radicals.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lentils.

items.title: Preservative content
items.content: Although sodium is reduced, canned products may contain additives that some people are sensitive to.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause increased gas in people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Certain varieties may contain a small amount of added sugar; check the label if you monitor sugar intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the soup in the microwave or on the stove until boiling, optionally add fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or a drizzle of olive oil to enhance flavor. Serve with whole‑grain bread or crackers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer any leftovers to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
